assumptions: Assume access to consistent source-cell conditioned medium lots for method comparison.
Assume immuno-capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation have sufficient sensitivity for the expected particle concentrations.
biological_rationale: Rodent intranasal efficacy reports motivate defining a producible intact-EV drug substance. MISEV2023 emphasizes orthogonal intact-EV analytics to distinguish EV-enriched fractions from secretome. Demonstrating that a scalable fractionation workflow yields an analytically distinct, membrane-protected, particle-associated fraction will enable a reproducible product identity for CMC development and potency assay linkage rather than reliance on unbounded secretome concentrates (inference; uncertainty labeled).

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Orthogonal intact-EV assay panel (capture + particle co-localization + membrane-protection)
candidate_quality_attributes.name: EV identity and purity
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Use orthogonal intact-EV signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity) to qualify the bounded small-EV fraction as the drug-substance identity attribute for CMC decisions.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: Moderate: required to be demonstrated in program-specific materials; MISEV guidance supports orthogonal panels but not exact workflow.

edges.competing_explanation: An apparent capture-positive co-localization could reflect residual non-vesicular particles (lipoproteins/aggregates) that co-elute in the chosen SEC/iodixanol window.
edges.missing_experiment: Program-specific demonstration that the proposed two-step, scalable workflow produces a membrane-protected, capture-positive particle peak distinct from secretome concentrate and with acceptable yield metrics.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV recommends orthogonal characterization and suggests fractionation state matters for identity and potency, but does not specify that a TFF→SEC→single-cushion workflow will preserve membrane-protected signatures at manufacturing yields.

edges.competing_explanation: Lack of CNS detection in macaque might be due to administration, labeling, or species clearance differences rather than fractionation state.
edges.missing_experiment: Orthogonal intact-EV verification from materials produced by the scalable workflow tested in short-interval in vivo dosing to confirm detectability in relevant compartments.
edges.uncertainty: High: large-animal negative biodistribution suggests delivery/exposure risks that make establishing a reproducible drug-substance identity even more critical for subsequent bridging studies.

nodes.statement: A scalable fractionation workflow (TFF → SEC → single-step iodixanol cushion) can produce a size- and density-bounded fraction with a membrane-protected, particle-associated analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle-count peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity).

The concentrated conditioned-medium (secretome-retaining) processed only by TFF concentration lacks the co-localized capture-positive particle peak and shows marker signal that is largely detergent/protease-insensitive, consistent with non-vesicular co-isolates.

If n1 is true and yields are manufacturable, the bounded small-EV fraction can serve as a reproducible drug-substance definition to support orthogonal QC and potency assay development (inference; uncertainty noted).

competing_explanations: Co-localized capture-positive signal may reflect co-isolated non-vesicular particles (lipoproteins, aggregates) rather than bona fide membrane-enclosed EVs.
Manufacturable yields may be insufficient even if orthogonal signature is observed, forcing a tradeoff between identity and scale.
dependencies: Define source-cell lot and ensure matched conditioned-medium production (same bank/passage range)
Secure validated immuno-capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation
Establish simple yield acceptance rubric for manufacturability benchmarking (qualitative at this stage)
design_question: Daily question: Can a scalable two-step fractionation (tangential-flow concentration + size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) followed by a limited iodixanol cushion that preserves yield) produce a reproducible intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity) that is absent from a concentrated secretome and is compatible with reasonable manufacturing yield?
expected_measurable_effect: Orthogonal analytical differentiation: the bounded small-EV fraction will show particle-count peaks that co-localize with capture-positive signal and marked loss of captured signal after detergent + protease/RNase treatment, while the concentrated secretome retains marker signal that does not co-localize with particle peaks and is largely insensitive to membrane disruption; yield (mass/particle recovery) will meet predefined manufacturability thresholds (qualitative for this proposal).

experiment.assay: Orthogonal workflow: (1) perform density-fractionation of the candidate fraction (single-cushion fractions) with particle counting per fraction; (2) immuno-capture ELISA/bead-capture detection of EV surface markers on intact fractions; (3) protease/RNase protection ± detergent on captured material; (4) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction; (5) measure manufacturing yield metrics (mass and particle recovery) across workflows.
experiment.comparator: Matched preparations from the same conditioned-medium lot: (A) TFF-concentrated secretome-retaining material (no SEC/cushion) versus (B) TFF→SEC→single-step iodixanol-cushion bounded small-EV fraction.
experiment.control: Negative controls: buffer-only, detergent-disrupted captured material. Positive control: commercially available characterized small EVs or lab-validated small-EV preparation (if available) to verify capture and particle-count co-localization behavior.
dependencies: Availability of consistent source-cell conditioned-medium lots (same passage/bank)
Access to capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation
Analytical capacity for single-step iodixanol cushion fractionation and rapid particle counting
experiment.failure_criterion: No qualitative difference between the bounded small-EV fraction and concentrated secretome in co-localization or membrane-protection behavior across replicates, or yields are consistently inadequate for manufacturing considerations.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If failure criteria are met, the hypothesis is falsified: the proposed scalable fractionation does not produce an analytically distinct intact-EV drug-substance candidate and the program should treat the material as indistinguishable from secretome for product-definition and prioritize alternative isolation strategies or secretome-centric product definitions.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: A scalable, two-step fractionation (TFF→SEC→single-step iodixanol cushion) yields a size-and-density-bounded fraction with a membrane-protected, particle-associated analytical signature that is absent from concentrated secretome, while providing acceptable yield for manufacturing consideration.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative co-localization of particle-count peaks with capture-positive fractions and demonstrable loss of captured signal after detergent + protease/RNase treatment in the bounded small-EV fraction but not in the concentrated secretome; plus qualitative assessment of yield (recovery sufficient to support GMP-like batch considerations).
experiment.question: Can the proposed scalable fractionation workflow (TFF concentration → SEC → single-step iodixanol cushion) produce a bounded small-EV fraction that (A) displays an orthogonal intact-EV signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive signal) and (B) achieves manufacturable yield compared with a concentrated secretome control?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium (same source-cell lot) processed into: (A) TFF-concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) and (B) TFF → SEC → single-step iodixanol cushion bounded fraction from the same lot
Immuno-capture reagents (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5 capture reagents)
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Iodixanol materials for a single-step cushion
Total protein assay reagents and equipment to measure mass recovery
Buffers and consumables for SEC and TFF
secondary_readouts: Protein:particle ratio differences between the bounded fraction and the secretome control
Reproducibility across biological replicates (n ≥ 3 independent conditioned-medium lots)
Mass and particle recovery percentages for each workflow
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: In ≥ 3 independent conditioned-medium lots, the TFF→SEC→single-step cushion fraction shows a particle-count peak that co-localizes with capture-positive signal and the captured signal is substantially reduced after detergent + protease/RNase, whereas the TFF-concentrated secretome shows marker signal that does not co-localize with particle peaks and is largely detergent/protease-insensitive; yield estimates indicate recovery sufficient for preliminary GMP-like batch scale considerations (qualitative pass).

explicit_inferences: Inference: Orthogonal membrane-protection and particle-co-localization are necessary analytical observations to classify a fraction as an intact-EV-enriched drug-substance rather than unpurified secretome.

Inference: A two-step, scalable fractionation workflow (TFF→SEC→single-step iodixanol cushion) is a plausible manufacturable route to obtain a bounded small-EV fraction for CMC development, but program-specific validation is required.
falsification_criteria: Across n ≥ 3 independent conditioned-medium lots, the scalable TFF→SEC→single-cushion fraction fails to show reproducible co-localization of particle-count peaks with capture-positive signal and/or captured signal is not reduced by detergent + protease/RNase (i.e., material lacks membrane-protected behavior), and analytical profiles are indistinguishable from concentrated secretome controls; or yields are consistently insufficient for manufacturable recovery.
human_decisions_required: Approve use of TFF→SEC→single-cushion workflow for program-scale method comparison
Set qualitative or quantitative yield thresholds that would be considered 'manufacturable' for next decision steps
manufacturability_assessment: The proposed workflow prioritizes scalable unit operations (TFF, SEC) plus a single density cushion rather than research ultracentrifugation; this increases plausibility of translation to GMP-like runs but requires experimental yield and recovery benchmarking (evidence_gap).
manufacturing_rationale: A two-step workflow (TFF concentration to enable scalable handling, followed by SEC to remove bulk soluble proteins, and a single-step iodixanol cushion to enrich particle-containing density range) is more likely to be manufacturable at scale than ultracentrifugation-based lab workflows while preserving an orthogonal intact-EV signature if such a signature is present (inference; uncertainty labeled).
measurement_strategy: Orthogonal intact-EV analytical panel applied to matched materials: (1) density-fraction particle counts, (2) immuno-capture ELISA/bead-capture for canonical EV surface markers on intact fractions, (3) detergent + protease/RNase protection on captured material, (4) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction, plus yield metrics (mass, particle recovery) after the scalable workflow.
novelty_statement: Novel: This hypothesis couples an explicitly scalable, minimal-density-step fractionation (TFF→SEC→single-step iodixanol cushion) to an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture + particle co-localization + detergent/protease protection) and adds manufacturability (yield) as a gating dimension. Prior program hypotheses focused on analytical discrimination using laboratory enrichment methods (ultracentrifugation/SEC) or on source-cell senescence or potency linkage; this proposal uniquely tests a translation-minded fractionation process that is deliberately constrained to one density step and includes yield benchmarking to resolve the product-definition tradeoff between identity and manufacturability.
principal_risks: Risk that the scalable workflow fails to produce an orthogonal intact-EV signature distinct from secretome (evidence_gap).
Risk that observed capture-positive signals reflect non-vesicular co-isolates (competing explanation).
Risk that yields are too low for GMP-like production despite favorable analytics.
proposed_potency_relationship: If an intact-EV-enriched, membrane-protected fraction is identified and reproducibly recovered with manufacturable yield, that fraction will be used as the prioritized input for subsequent potency-linkage experiments (inference; separate experiments required).
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt a manufacturable fractionation gate: a size-and-density-bounded small-EV drug-substance fraction (produced by TFF concentration → SEC → single-step iodixanol cushion) that shows an orthogonal intact-EV signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive signal) and meets yield criteria to be treated as the drug-substance for downstream CMC decisions.
title: Hypothesis: A defined size-and-density-bounded small-EV fraction recovered by scalable SEC+density-gradient yields an orthogonal intact-EV signature absent in concentrated secretome, enabling a manufacturable fractionation gate
